editorialNarrative.synopsis: Sabah and Hapoel Beer-Sheva have reached the decisive second leg, with one of the remaining league-phase places attached to the tie. Qualification filled the final seven places in the 36-team league phase, with LASK producing the stage's lasting recovery: a 5–1 extra-time return-leg win after losing 3–0 at Celtic. Sabah and Slovan Bratislava also survived extra time, and all seven winners now persist as named entrants in the next phase rather than disappearing with the completed bracket.

editorialNarrative.hook: Eight matchdays determine which clubs skip February and which must take the knockout play-off route.
editorialNarrative.synopsis: Eight matchdays determine which clubs skip February and which must take the knockout play-off route. The league phase asks each of 36 clubs to face eight different opponents across 144 matches. AEK Athens v LASK opens a direct line from qualification, while first-time Champions League entrant LASK and first-time European participant Como enter the same table as back-to-back champion Paris Saint-Germain. The opening story is continuity, not a blank group-stage reset.

editorialNarrative.hook: One match in Madrid decides the European champion after every qualifying and knockout route converges.
editorialNarrative.synopsis: One match in Madrid decides the European champion after every qualifying and knockout route converges. The 36-team league table determines three distinct fates and also shapes play-off seeding. The knockout path begins in February and ends at Estadio Metropolitano, while Paris's pursuit of a third consecutive title remains a live thread rather than an assumed participant outcome.
